title: Major depression: episode, severity and remission
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM code for the patient's depressive disorder.
note:
Chief Complaint
Evaluation of depression.

HPI
The patient is a 79-year-old female presenting for a follow-up evaluation of her mental health. She reports a persistent low mood and a significant lack of interest in activities she previously enjoyed. She describes a profound sense of fatigue and a feeling of heaviness throughout the day. She reports that she has been experiencing a single episode of depression that has significantly impacted her ability to perform daily tasks. She notes that her sleep has been disrupted, characterized by early morning awakening and difficulty falling asleep. She denies any perceptual disturbances or a break from reality. The patient describes her current symptoms as severe, noting that she feels overwhelmed by her daily responsibilities and feels a sense of hopelessness regarding her future. She reports anhedonia and a decrease in appetite over the last month.

Review of Systems
Constitutional: Fatigue, poor appetite.
Psychiatric: Depressed mood, anhedonia.
Neurological: None.
All other systems reviewed and are negative.

Social History
The patient is retired and lives with her spouse in a single-family home. She enjoys gardening and knitting. She denies any tobacco or alcohol use.

Family History
Mother had hypertension. Father had a history of coronary artery disease. No known history of psychiatric conditions in immediate family.

Medication List
Sertraline 50mg daily
Lisinopril 10mg daily

Vitals
Temperature: 98.6 F
Blood Pressure: 128/82 mmHg
Heart Rate: 74 bpm
Respiratory Rate: 16 breaths/min
SpO2: 98% on room air
Weight: 145 lbs

Recent Labs
Hemoglobin: 13.2 g/dL
White Blood Cell Count: 7.2 x 10^9/L
TSH: 2.1 mIU/L
Glucose: 105 mg/dL

Exam
The patient appears neatly groomed but has a flat affect. She is cooperative and maintains good eye contact. Speech is normal in rate and volume. Cognition is intact, and she is oriented to person, place, and time. Mood is described as "sad." Thought process is linear and goal-directed. No evidence of formal thought disorder.

Assessment
The patient is presenting with major depressive disorder, single episode. The current presentation is severe without psychotic features.

Plan
Continue current dosage of Sertraline. The patient will continue to monitor symptoms and report any significant changes. Follow-up in four weeks to reassess the severity of her symptoms and medication efficacy.

Electronically signed, D. Kowalski, NP, 05/14/2026
explanations: Major depressive disorder, single episode, severe without psychotic features (HCC 155): F32.2.
